line.text: Every Chancellor wants one thing in the speech nobody saw coming. Each of these is already costed on the desk; the cost is the headroom it leaves you on the morning after. Keeping the headroom is an announcement too, and the markets hear it.

options.title: A penny off the basic rate of income tax

line.text: The classic. It reaches every basic-rate taxpayer and, on HMRC’s own figures, costs more than most of your package put together. Everyone in the chamber knows the trick and everyone cheers anyway.

options.title: Free school meals for every child

line.text: Visible in every primary school by next September, and the means test goes with it. The Department for Education already funds infant meals; this is the rest of the school.
Fuel duty has not risen since 2011-12 and the last Budget kept the 5p cut going. A further cut is cheap per driver, dear in total, and the motoring lobby will bank it and ask again.
A billion a year sounds like a plan for the future and costs less than a penny on anything. It is the kind of announcement that reads well and is hard to see on the ground.
Going one notch beyond what you agreed with the Prime Minister turns a promise kept into a promise exceeded. Ministers notice the difference; so does the department that has to spend it.
No rabbit. The headroom is the announcement, and the bond market is the audience that hears it. Budget 2025 made a virtue of more than doubling the margin; you can make the same speech.
